title: Research: connect coordinate-SWAP handoffs to the existing cut theorem
body:
The five-SWAP handoff in PR2317 leaves a noncommuting thirteen-call candidate open, and `four-swap-full-occupancy` leaves four-SWAP dirty-workspace compression open. Both follow from the existing PR1989 theorem: the explicit action of GL2(F2) on its three nonzero vectors maps the two paid coordinate CNOTs to adjacent transpositions in S3 and SWAP to its three-inversion reversal. The exact formal cost is therefore **3t for every finite R >= t**, including noncommuting rank-one projectors, interleaved free scalar mixing and restored arbitrary dirty spectators. Five SWAPs require 15 calls; four require 12.

This package contributes an audited model bridge and a retrievable answer to those handoffs. It credits PR1989 for the general theorem and cut method; it makes no new general lower-bound, supplier, recursive moment or kappa claim. The written proof binds the full group algebra, gate prices and complete endpoint. Historical predecessor files and the selected record are unchanged. The scope change from the drawn bit-mechanisms card is explicit in TASK.json.

Validation at head `7b9997ba2ca13be75dfc423642e2ce6b8ed18d6e`:

- Registered Python 3.12 optimized replay passes, including the primary full-coefficient checker, a code-disjoint faithful regular-action checker, and nine behavioral control groups. The two checkers cover 27 and 18 complete dirty endpoints; the independent engine also checks every rank-one projector through seven roles and 14 interleaved noncommuting fixtures. Exact finite domains are recorded in the README and REVIEW.md.
- Actual endpoint-guard removal, rank/label faults, source corruption/missing inputs and dirty coupling reject. Equivalent group-basis ordering and read-only Git-free relocation with the pinned sources pass. Primary normal Python 3.12 and optimized Python 3.14 checks also pass.
- Source pins, metadata, selected-record integrity and staged whitespace pass. No full selected cold replay, physical compilation or formal-kernel/human proof review is claimed; hosted CI is separate.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gl2-swap-cut-corollary`.

Pins: canonical base `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4; PR1989 `8b9f3ec8b1e5745c42fec68d75da5fbc82ea91ec` (proof byte-identical on main); PR2317 `139779c86ba8215910117ddb383e4df007b23dcf` (model read and head rechecked). The prepublication refresh left main/guidance/selected hash unchanged. Final overlap covered 617 open PRs including drafts and 1,140 Discussion records at 08:12–08:15 UTC, with complete pagination and no warnings; local notes/TASK/ledger were included. This is not a novelty certificate.

[Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18944151). Credits: Aaron Wang's PR2317 handoff, Ross Richardson's PR1989 and four-SWAP lineage, Adam Gall's cut-method work, and the retained Gareth Davidson/commdata2338/Cinna Davis predecessors. Prepared by Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including a separate mathematical verifier. Apache-2.0. Future work must change a named operation, tariff or endpoint premise before another same-model sharing search.
